test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 10 Sept, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is NOT correct with regards to the history of calculating National Income (NI) in India?

options.text: First attempt to compute NI was made by Dadabhai Naoroji.
First official attempt to compute NI was made by PC Mahalanobis.
Dadabhai Naoroji divided the Indian economy into two parts: primary sector and secondary sector.
First scientific method to compute NI was used by Dr VKRV Rao.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Dadabhai Naoroji divided the Indian economy into two parts: primary sector and secondary sector**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• National income is the total income of all the residents of the country.
 
• Thus, it is the total income of the country.
 
• It is considered to be one of the most important attributes for comparing the development of countries.
 
• The National Income formula equals GDP + Foreign Production by National Residents – Domestic Production by Non-National Residents.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji**

 
• Dadabhai Naoroji, known as the Grand Old Man of India, was a leading figure in the early Indian independence movement and a founder of the Indian National Congress.
 
 
• His activities were mainly in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.
 
• The Indian Independence League, however, was primarily active during the 1940s, significantly after Naoroji's most impactful years and following his death in 1917.
 
• This organization sought to obtain independence for India from British rule during World War II, with notable connections to Subhas Chandra Bose and the Indian National Army (INA).
 
• Naoroji founded or was associated with several organizations, like the Bombay Association (the oldest political organization in Bombay), the East India Association (established in London to discuss Indian affairs), and Gyan Prasarak Mandali (for the education of adult men in Bombay).
 
• These affiliations reflected his focus on political advocacy, economic theories (notably the Drain Theory), and social reform both in India and the UK.
 
• The Indian Independence League's context and methods, focused on leveraging the geopolitical situations during World War II for India's independence through more direct action, were distinct and not within Naoroji's lifetime or direct activities.
 
 
 
• **​PC Mahalanobis**
 
 
• The Second five-year plan was based on the Mahalanobis model, an economic development model developed by the Indian statistician Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis in 1953.
 
• PC Mahalanobis established the Indian Statistical Institute (ISI) in Calcutta in 1931 and for the same reason, he is known as the father of Indian Statistics. He was a member of the first Planning Commission of free India.
 
• The second five-year plan was for the year 1956-1961.
 
• The second five-year plan focused on the development of the public sector and rapid Industrialisation. The plan attempted to determine a balanced allocation of investment between productive sectors in order to maximize long-run economic growth. 
 
• As a result, hydroelectric power projects across the country and five steel plants at Bhilai, Durgapur, and Rourkela were established with the help of Russia, Britain (the U.K), and West Germany respectively. Coal production was increased. More railway lines were added all over the country.
 
• The Tata Institute of Fundamental Research and Atomic Energy Commission of India was established to promote research in India.
